# narrata

> An embedded, local-first narration runtime for Go. Narrata turns structured events into in-character narration text (and optional speech) using pluggable, offline-friendly backends.

narrata is importable as `github.com/danielriddell21/narrata` (the public library lives at the module root). It ships with deterministic, dependency-free text backends; the llama.cpp and kokoro backends are opt-in behind build tags.

The central type is the Engine:

```go
type Engine struct{ /* ... */ }

func New(cfg Config) (*Engine, error)
func (e *Engine) Generate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error)
func (e *Engine) Personas() PersonaStore
func (e *Engine) Close() error
```

A minimal call:

```go
eng, _ := narrata.New(narrata.Config{Text: narrata.TextConfig{Backend: "template"}})
defer eng.Close()
res, _ := eng.Generate(ctx, narrata.Request{Event: "door_opened", Output: narrata.OutputText})
fmt.Println(res.Text)
```

Personas drive the voice. `narrata.GeneratePersona(description)` scaffolds one from free text; persona files are validated on load. The `narrata` CLI (`cmd/narrata`) wraps the same library for validating, generating, and listing personas.
